subject.title: Add optional `name`/`label` field to group config entries

question: Should OpenClaw add a single display-only `label` field across stable-ID-keyed channel group-entry contracts, and which channel entry shapes are in scope for the first supported contract?
rationale: This creates a public config surface across heterogeneous channel schemas; maintainers must choose its permanent name and scope before a mechanical implementation can be safely defined.

options.title: Adopt `label` for stable-ID group entries
options.body: Define `label?: string` as ignored display metadata for the audited group/channel-entry shapes, with no runtime matching or authorization effect.

options.title: Limit the initial contract to Telegram
options.body: Add the annotation only to Telegram group entries now and retain a tracked cross-channel design decision for the remaining schemas.

options.title: Decline config annotations
options.body: Keep stable identifiers as the only supported group-entry keys and improve discovery or configuration UX through a separate product path.

recommendation.title: Adopt `label` for stable-ID group entries
recommendation.body: Define `label?: string` as ignored display metadata for the audited group/channel-entry shapes, with no runtime matching or authorization effect.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history and current discussion place this person closest to the shared channel configuration boundary.
